landmarks.name: Wawel Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic castle residency in Kraków, symbolizing Polish national identity and royal heritage.

landmarks.name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
landmarks.writeup: The largest Nazi concentration and extermination camp, now a museum and memorial site.

landmarks.name: Old Town Warsaw
landmarks.writeup: Reconstructed historic center of Warsaw, showcasing Polish resilience and architectural heritage.

landmarks.name: Malbork Castle
landmarks.writeup: The largest brick castle in the world, built by the Teutonic Knights in the 13th century.

landmarks.name: Bianowiena Forest
landmarks.writeup: One of the last and largest remaining parts of the primeval forest that once covered Europe.

cultural_events.name: Wianki Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A midsummer celebration in Kraków featuring music, traditional rituals, and floating wreaths on the river.

cultural_events.name: Kraków Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: One of Europe's oldest film festivals, focusing on documentary, animation, and short films.

cultural_events.name: Saint Dominic's Fair
cultural_events.writeup: A historic trade and cultural fair held annually in Gdansk since the 13th century.

food_writeup: Polish cuisine features hearty dishes such as pierogi (dumplings), bigos (hunter's stew), and kielbasa (sausage), reflecting a blend of Eastern and Central European culinary traditions.
brief_history: Poland has a rich history dating back over a thousand years, marked by the establishment of the Polish state in 966, partitions by neighboring powers in the late 18th century, regaining independence in 1918, devastation during World War II, and a transition from communism to democracy in 1989.

important_people.name: Marie Curie
important_people.description: Physicist and chemist, Nobel Prize laureate

important_people.name: Lech Wannsa
important_people.description: Leader of Solidarity movement and former president

important_people.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
important_people.description: Renaissance astronomer who formulated heliocentric theory

current_conflicts: Poland is not engaged in any active military conflicts but is involved in regional security efforts as a NATO member, particularly in response to tensions in Eastern Europe.
